newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech later-than-expected in long distance.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech later-than-expected in long distance.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Thursday it will not commercially launch its long distance telephone service before April 1997.
Ameritech, one of the regional Bell operating companies, had previously said it expected to enter the lucrative market during the first quarter of 1997.

Richard Notebaert, talking to reporters during a monthly meeting, said the company will file right after the first of the year the necessary forms with the Federal Communications Commission, as required by the Telecommunications Act.
The FCC then has 90 days to reply, he said.
"It would have to be in April," Notebaert said. "Putting it (filing) together took a little longer, so we're probably a few months late."

In an interview in October, Notebaert said the company planned to begin providing long distance service during the first quarter of 1997. But he cautioned that Ameritech had to be flexible as its entrance was dependent upon certain FCC rules which were being challenged in court by other phone companies.
